plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period parchment, an inked diagram compares pure gold (density 19.32 g/cm³, 1,000 g = 51.8 cm³) against a 1,000 g crown mixed with 30% silver (density 10.49 g/cm³, volume = 64.8 cm³): in a 30 cm basin, the 13.1 cm³ difference raises the water level by just 0.18 mm (invisible under surface tension), whereas on Archimedes' and Galileo's 1586 underwater balance the extra 13.1 cm³ of displaced water pushes up on the crown with 13.1 grams of extra buoyant force.

teach_overlay.label: 1,000 G GOLD (51.8 CM³) VS 70/30 CROWN (64.8 CM³): 0.18 MM RISE VS 13.1 G LIFT
teach_overlay.detail: Inked comparison diagram on period paper showing 1,000 g pure gold (51.8 cm³) vs 1,000 g 70/30 crown (64.8 cm³): a 13.1 cm³ (<1 tbsp) difference that raises a 30 cm bowl by 0.18 mm, but tips an underwater balance by 13.1 g
teach_overlay.scale: 13 cubic centimetres of extra volume is less than one tablespoon of water — raising a wide bowl by less than two sheets of paper, yet tipping an underwater scale by 13 full grams
teach_overlay.who_card: Archimedes of Syracuse (~287–212 BC) — Greek mathematician and physicist · King Hiero II (~308–215 BC) — Greek ruler of Syracuse · Galileo Galilei (1564–1642) — Italian mathematician and physicist
